newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-McGuigan Wines to raise A$7.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-McGuigan Wines to raise A$7.5 mln.

text.p: Wine-maker Brian McGuigan Wines Ltd said on Friday it would raise about A$7.5 million through a 1-for-4 renounceable rights issue at A$1.00 per share to fund the acquisition of a Hunter Valley winery and to reduce debt.
The issue is being underwritten by Prudential Bache Securities Australia and Bridges Financial Services.

"The funds raised by the issue which together with the concurrent A$2.3 million placement and the A$2.8 million raised through the exercise of options by interests associated with Brian McGuigan, will enable the company to acquire the Hunter Estate Winery, to reduce debt and meet the challenges of the next three years," Brian McGuigan Wines said.
The company said it would buy the Hunter Estate Winery at Polkobin from Orlando Wyndham Pty Ltd for A$3.6 million.

"The acquisition of the winery was necessary to meet the growing sales volume both domestically and internationally and the acquisition of the winery will establish for the company a modern processing facility with sufficient capacity to cope with the company's current planned processing requirements through to the year 2000," it said.
The rights and other issues would allow Brian McGuigan Wines to signifantly reduce bank and other debt.
"The reduction in gearing will allow the company to continue to pursue a vigorous strategy for growth."
Brian McGuigan Wines said the recent severe hailstorms in the Hunter region have not damaged any of the company's vineyards.

Brian McGuigan's exercise of options and his subsequent sale of 1.2 million shares to current shareholder James Smiley would result in McGuigan keeping his stake in the company at about 20 percent and Smiley increasing his stake to about 10 percent.
Brian McGuigan's shares were down one cent at A$1.26 at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).
